newsitem.title: USA: Clinton doubtful of apology to blacks for slavery.
newsitem.headline: Clinton doubtful of apology to blacks for slavery.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is not actively considering whether the United States should apologise to black Americans for enslaving their ancestors, the White House said on Tuesday.
When he launched in June a year-long initiative on ways to breach the racial divide, Clinton had said he needed time to decide whether the government should formally apologise to blacks for slavery.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry gave a strong indication at his daily news briefing that an apology would not be forthcoming any time soon, if at all.
"The president has, really, in a way, put that issue aside and said that's not going to be the focus of his race initiative," McCurry said.
A seven-member advisory board that Clinton appointed to make recommendations on ways to mend relations between the races has said it would look at the apology question, which McCurry said was proper.
But he said Clinton has had many conversations with people in the black community and that often he hears an apology is not an issue to dwell on in the race initiative.

"He's had lots of conversations with people, and very few have suggested that that's the critical issue that ought to be at the centre of this process or that it be the issue that begins the work that he intends to do," he said.

A proposal by Ohio Democratic Representative Tony Hall for a congressional apology for slavery has generated strong emotions. Some whites feel it brings up an ugly chapter in America's past. Some blacks would want an apology coupled with compensation, the way Japanese-Americans were compensated for being held in detention camps in the Second World War.
House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich of Georgia has scoffed at the proposed apology, calling it "emotional symbolism" that avoided tackling real problems.

Clinton, a son of the South who witnessed the civil rights upheavals of the 1960s, has been a vocal advocate of repairing race relations and wants his initiative to concentrate on such issues as improving education for blacks and ending discrimination.
